answer: A collateral-bonding protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital in an escrow haven before clearing workloads through a network wharf. To forge multiple identities, an adversary must commit scarce financial liquidity across an extended staking horizon, incurring substantial opportunity costs and slashing exposure per identity. However, this defense imposes severe capital barriers on underfunded agents and disproportionately favors wealthy actors.
